Elsewhere in scripture

nodes.t: Proverbs: overview
nodes.d: Proverbs begins with the proverbs of Solomon son of David (1:1), sets out a father’s teaching about wisdom and folly (1-9), gathers many short sayings (10-29), and ends with the words of Agur (30) and of king Lemuel (31).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the main sections of Proverbs and who is named as the source of each?
ev: Describe the main sections of Proverbs: 1-9, 10-22, 22-24, 25-29, 30, 31.

nodes.t: The purpose of Proverbs and the fear of the LORD
nodes.d: Proverbs is given to know wisdom and instruction, to give prudence to the simple and knowledge to the young, and it names the fear of the LORD as the beginning of knowledge while fools despise wisdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Proverbs 1:7 and explain it in their own words?
ev: Name what Proverbs 1:2-4 says the book is for and what 1:7 calls the beginning of knowledge.

nodes.t: Do not follow sinners; wisdom cries out
nodes.d: A father urges his son to hear instruction and not consent when sinners entice him to join violence; Wisdom cries in the streets and warns those who hate knowledge and refuse her reproof.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the two warnings in Proverbs 1: the sinners’ enticing and Wisdom’s rebuke?
ev: Describe the enticement of 1:10-14 and the warning of 1:24-33.

nodes.t: Seeking wisdom: protection and the right path
nodes.d: The father says that if the son seeks wisdom like silver he will understand the fear of the LORD, and wisdom will deliver him from evil men and from the strange woman and keep him on the way of good men.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the son must do and what he will receive in Proverbs 2?
ev: List what Proverbs 2 says the LORD gives and what wisdom keeps the son from.

nodes.t: Trust in the LORD with all your heart
nodes.d: The father tells his son to keep his commandments, trust in the LORD and not lean on his own understanding, accept the LORD’s correction, value wisdom above silver and gold, and do good to his neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 3:5-6 and give one example of leaning on one’s own understanding?
ev: Read 3:5-6 and say what the son is told to do and what the LORD does.
Find 3:11-12 and say what it says about correction.

nodes.t: Get wisdom; guard your heart
nodes.d: A father recalls the teaching he received, tells his son to get wisdom and understanding, to avoid the path of the wicked, and to keep his heart with all diligence since the issues of life flow from it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain 4:23 and name the two paths described in chapter 4?
ev: Contrast the paths in 4:14-19 and 4:18.
Say what 4:23 tells the son to guard.

nodes.t: Warnings against the strange woman
nodes.d: The father warns his son against the strange woman whose lips drop honey but whose end is bitter and whose feet go down to death, and urges him to find joy in the wife of his youth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the warning of Proverbs 5 and the counsel given in 5:15-19?
ev: Read Proverbs 5:3-6 and 5:15-19 and contrast the warning with the counsel.

nodes.t: Surety, sloth and seven abominations
nodes.d: Proverbs warns against becoming surety for a neighbour, sends the sluggard to the ant, describes the froward man who sows discord, and lists six things the LORD hates, even seven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some of the seven things the LORD hates in Proverbs 6:16-19?
ev: List the six things and the seventh named in 6:16-19.
Say what the ant teaches in 6:6-8.

nodes.t: Keep the commandment; the snare of adultery
nodes.d: The father says the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, warns that adultery brings ruin and burning that cannot be hidden, and in chapter 7 tells how a simple young man is lured by a woman and walks to her house like an ox to the slaughter.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the scene in Proverbs 7 and the warning it ends with?
ev: Describe the young man’s steps in 7:6-23 and the closing warning in 7:24-27.

nodes.t: Wisdom calls aloud and was there at creation
nodes.d: Wisdom cries out to the simple, says she is better than rubies, loves those who love her, and describes herself as brought forth by the LORD before the earth and rejoicing when he set the heavens and the foundations of the earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Wisdom says about herself in Proverbs 8:22-31?
ev: Read 8:22-31 and say what Wisdom says about her place before and during creation.
List what Wisdom offers in 8:12-21.

nodes.t: Two invitations: Wisdom’s house and Folly’s seat
nodes.d: Wisdom builds a house, prepares a feast and calls the simple to come, while a foolish woman sits at her door and calls them to stolen waters; the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare the invitation of Wisdom and the invitation of the foolish woman in Proverbs 9?
ev: Compare the two invitations in 9:1-6 and 9:13-18.
Read 9:10.

nodes.t: Proverbs of Solomon: the righteous, the wicked and words (10-11)
nodes.d: Short sayings contrast the righteous and the wicked, the diligent and the lazy, and the mouth that gives life with the mouth that harms; chapter 11 adds sayings on integrity, pride, surety and generosity.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} pick one saying from Proverbs 10 or 11 and explain what two ways of life it contrasts?
ev: Collect three contrasts between righteous and wicked from chapter 10 and chapter 11.

nodes.t: Fools, counsel, truth and diligence (12-13)
nodes.d: The sayings praise truthful lips over lying tongues, the one who hears counsel over the fool who is right in his own eyes, and diligent work over slothfulness; chapter 13 speaks about the mouth, wealth and discipline.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 12:15 and give a saying from chapters 12-13 about work?
ev: Find a saying about speech, one about work, and one about counsel in chapters 12-13.

nodes.t: The fear of the LORD, the simple and the prudent (14-15)
nodes.d: The sayings contrast the simple who believe every word with the prudent who consider their steps, call the fear of the LORD a fountain of life, say that oppressing the poor insults their Maker, and teach that a soft answer turns away wrath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 15:1 and give an example from daily life?
ev: Read 14:27, 14:31 and 15:1 and say what each teaches.

nodes.t: The LORD directs; pride and strife (16-17)
nodes.d: The sayings say a man’s plans are before the LORD, that pride goes before destruction, that the LORD tries hearts as a furnace tries gold, and that justifying the wicked or condemning the just is an abomination to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 16:18 and name one saying about the LORD’s part in human plans in chapter 16?
ev: Read 16:3, 16:18 and 17:15 and state the lesson of each.

nodes.t: The tongue, friends, anger, rich and poor (18-19)
nodes.d: The sayings warn that a fool’s mouth is his destruction, that death and life are in the power of the tongue, that a brother offended is hard to win, that discretion defers anger, and that the poor are often forsaken while the fear of the LORD leads to life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 18:21 in their own words?
ev: Read 18:21 and 19:11 and say what each teaches.

nodes.t: Honest weights, justice and the safety of the LORD (20-21)
nodes.d: The sayings say wine is a mocker, that divers weights are an abomination to the LORD, that doing justice is more acceptable to him than sacrifice, and that the horse is prepared for battle but safety is of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 21:3 and say why it matters?
ev: Read 20:23, 21:3 and 21:31 and state what each says.

nodes.t: Good name, training a child, and the poor (22:1-16)
nodes.d: The sayings praise a good name over riches, say the rich and poor meet before their maker, tell parents to train up a child in his way, and say the rich rule over the poor while the borrower is servant to the lender.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 22:6 and name something from 22:1-16 about the poor?
ev: Read 22:1, 22:2 and 22:6 and say what each teaches.

nodes.t: Sayings of the wise: do not rob the poor, do not envy sinners
nodes.d: The writer calls the reader to bow the ear to the words of the wise so that trust may be in the LORD, forbids robbing the poor, warns against greed for riches, correction of a child, the drunkard and the winebibber, and urges buying truth and not envying sinners.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says is the reason for these sayings in Proverbs 22:17-21?
ev: Read 23:29-35 and describe the picture of strong drink.
Read 22:17-21 and say why the writer addresses the reader.

nodes.t: More sayings of the wise: wisdom, enemies and the sluggard’s field
nodes.d: The sayings say not to envy evil men, that wise men are strong, that respect of persons in judgment is not good, that one should not rejoice when an enemy falls or repay evil, and the writer learns a lesson from the field of the slothful man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Proverbs 24:17 and 24:29 say about enemies?
ev: Read 24:17-18 and 24:29 and say what each commands.
Retell what the writer sees in 24:30-34.

nodes.t: More proverbs of Solomon: kings, neighbours and fitting words (25)
nodes.d: These proverbs, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out, speak of the glory of God to conceal a thing and the honour of kings to search it out, a word fitly spoken, restraint with a neighbour, and kindness to an enemy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 25:1 says about the source of chapters 25-29 and give one saying from chapter 25?
ev: Read 25:1 and say who copied these proverbs.
Find the saying about a word fitly spoken (25:11).

nodes.t: Fools, sluggards and talebearers (26)
nodes.d: The proverbs liken honour for a fool to a stone bound in a sling, say a fool returns to his folly as a dog to its vomit, picture the slothful turning on his bed like a door on its hinges, and say strife ceases where there is no talebearer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list two pictures Proverbs 26 uses for a fool or a sluggard?
ev: Find three images used for the fool and the sluggard in chapter 26.

nodes.t: Friends, boasting and tending flocks (27)
nodes.d: The proverbs say not to boast of tomorrow or of yourself, that open rebuke is better than secret love, that iron sharpens iron, and that a man should know the state of his flocks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 27:17 and name one other saying about friends or boasting in chapter 27?
ev: Read 27:5-6 and 27:17 and explain the lesson on friendship.

nodes.t: Rulers, justice and confessing sin (28-29)
nodes.d: The proverbs say the wicked flee when no man pursues while the righteous are bold as a lion, that confessing and forsaking sin brings mercy, that the poor and the oppressed matter to rulers, that when the righteous rule the people rejoice, and that he who trusts his own heart is a fool.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 28:13 and give one saying about rulers from chapters 28-29?
ev: Read 28:13 and 29:2 and say what each teaches.
Contrast 28:26 with the proverbs on the fear of the LORD.

nodes.t: The words of Agur
nodes.d: Agur confesses he lacks understanding, asks who has ascended to heaven and gathered the wind, says every word of God is pure, asks for neither poverty nor riches, and lists things that are never satisfied or too wonderful and things that are small yet wise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Agur prays for in Proverbs 30:7-9?
ev: Read 30:5-9 and state what Agur asks of God.

nodes.t: The words of king Lemuel
nodes.d: King Lemuel recounts what his mother taught him: not to give his strength to women or to strong drink, and to open his mouth for the dumb and to plead for the poor and needy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Lemuel’s mother tells him about kings and the poor in Proverbs 31:1-9?
ev: Read 31:8-9 and say what the king is told to do for those who cannot speak for themselves.

nodes.t: The virtuous woman
nodes.d: A closing poem asks who can find a virtuous woman and describes her trust, work, care for her household and for the poor, and wise speech, concluding that a woman who fears the LORD shall be praised.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the woman of Proverbs 31 and read what 31:30 says is to be praised?
ev: List the works and character traits of the woman in 31:10-27.
Read 31:30 and say what is praised.

nodes.t: Romans: overview
nodes.d: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?
ev: State the letter's theme from 1:16-17
Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)

nodes.t: A living sacrifice
nodes.d: In view of God's mercies, believers present their bodies as a living sacrifice, are transformed by the renewing of the mind, and live in love as members of one body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 12:1-2?
ev: Explain 12:1-2
List ways Paul describes love in practice (12:9-21)

nodes.t: The Lord's discipline of his sons
nodes.d: The writer reminds readers that the Lord chastens those he loves as a father disciplines sons, for their profit and holiness, and that discipline afterwards yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the writer says God's discipline is a sign of sonship (12:5-11)?
ev: State why God chastens (12:6, 12:10)
Describe the result in 12:11

nodes.t: Hebrews: overview
nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)

nodes.t: James: overview
nodes.d: James is a letter from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, with practical teaching on trials, living faith, the tongue, humility, wealth and patience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what James tells believers to do with trials, words and wealth?
ev: Name the main themes of James in order
Say who the letter is from and to whom it is written

nodes.t: Conflicts, the world and humbling before God
nodes.d: James traces fightings to desires within, calls friendship with the world enmity with God, and says God gives grace to the humble, so believers must submit, resist the devil and draw near to God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do instead of fighting and loving the world?
ev: Say where James says wars and fightings come from
List the commands in 4:7-10
Explain what God does with the proud and the humble

nodes.t: 1 Peter: overview
nodes.d: 1 Peter is a letter from the apostle Peter to scattered strangers in Asia Minor, written to encourage them in suffering with the living hope, the example of Christ, holy conduct and humility under God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how 1 Peter encourages believers who suffer?
ev: Say who wrote 1 Peter and to whom
Name the main themes: hope, holiness, suffering and humility

nodes.t: Living to the will of God
nodes.d: Peter says believers who have the mind of Christ in suffering should end the old life of Gentile excess, live to God, and prepare for the end by prayer, fervent love, hospitality and using gifts for God's glory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list how Peter says to live because the end of all things is at hand?
ev: Describe the old life Peter says to leave behind
List the commands in 4:7-11
Explain why gifts are to be used for God's glory

nodes.t: The fiery trial and suffering as a Christian
nodes.d: Peter says not to be surprised by fiery trial but to rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings, not to suffer as an evildoer, and to entrust the soul to a faithful Creator while judgment begins at the house of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says not to be surprised by a fiery trial?
ev: Say how Peter tells believers to view fiery trials
Distinguish suffering as a Christian from suffering as an evildoer
Say whom believers entrust their souls to in 4:19

nodes.t: Shepherd the flock, humility and the roaring lion
nodes.d: Peter exhorts elders to shepherd willingly as examples with the chief Shepherd coming, tells all to be clothed with humility, cast cares on God, resist the devil who prowls like a roaring lion, and ends with greetings from Babylon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Peter tells elders and everyone else to do in chapter 5?
ev: Describe how elders are to lead in 5:2-3
Say what Peter tells believers to do with their cares
Say how Peter describes the devil and how to resist him

nodes.t: 2 Peter: overview
nodes.d: 2 Peter is a letter from Simon Peter urging growth in the knowledge of Christ, warning against false teachers and scoffers, and pointing to the certain day of the Lord and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 2 Peter warns about and what it tells believers to do?
ev: Name the three sections: growth, false teachers, the day of the Lord
Say what Peter wants believers to remember

nodes.t: The character and end of the false teachers
nodes.d: Peter describes the false teachers as presumptuous, greedy and following Balaam, promising freedom while enslaved to corruption, and says to return to the way of righteousness after knowing it is worse than never knowing it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Peter portrays the false teachers and why turning back is so serious?
ev: Name the charges in 2:13-15
Explain the saying about the dog and the sow in 2:22
Say who Peter compares them to in 2:15-16
